financing.summary: GL Homes is a private, family-controlled Florida builder (Ezratti family; The Real Deal's Sept. 2026 Forbes round-up put family wealth at $1.9B) that publishes no financial statements, has no SEC filings and no public or rated debt. It buys land outright and holds a long inventory: 4,871 acres at Indian Trails Grove entitled for 3,897 homes, the 4,000-acre Riverland master plan in Port St. Lucie, about 312 acres in Westlake bought for $109M, plus four closed golf courses. Public records reported by press show project-level acquisition mortgages from banks (Wells Fargo, City National Bank of Florida), mortgages to its own related entities, seller financing and per-home deferred payments to land sellers, rather than third-party land banks. The only land-bank-style capital on record is the 2010-2011 Mountain Real Estate Capital joint venture ($75M, 6,500 home sites), a downturn-era recapitalisation. Room for a land banker is narrow on core owned land, but 2026 spending is heavy (about $122M closed, $62.5M under contract and a further $40M Westlake tract due in 2027), and GL already buys finished-lot pods in other developers' master plans (Avenir, Arden, Westlake), which is the natural opening.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most and self-develops. President Misha Ezratti said in Sept. 2026 that GL holds an inventory of land, which lets it be selective, and in Nov. 2026 that it sticks to master-planned communities and agricultural land buyouts and goes after available land 'very hard'. Since Florida's Infill Redevelopment Act (2026) it has put a handful of qualifying sites (closed golf courses) under contract. It also buys finished-lot pods from master developers (Avenir, Arden, Westlake). No stated owned/optioned target; no public use of lot-option land banking.

lots.source_title: The Real Deal: Building the Sun Belt homebuilder roundtable
lots.note: No lot count is published (private). Pieces on the public record: Indian Trails Grove 4,871 acres owned, entitled for 3,897 homes (Town-Crier 2025-06); Westlake about 312 acres for 1,000+ homes, first plat 448 homes on 119.8 acres (TRD 2026-01, Town-Crier 2025-06); Calusa 524 homes approved 2026-04; Falls Club proposal 500 homes + 300 apartments (2025-12); Polo West 284 homes (under contract); Village Golf Club about 175 acres (plan not filed); Agave Boca 300+ townhomes and Orchid Isles at Avenir 42 sites (coming soon); Riverland 4,000 acres (a 2019 SFBJ profile put Port St. Lucie at about 11,000 lots, roughly 20 years; stale). Spine shows 1,617 closings, so owned supply is plainly many years.

land_banking.description: June 2010 equity joint venture of $75M to buy one new project and recapitalise six existing GL partnerships, covering 8,300+ acres and 6,500 home sites in West Palm Beach, Tampa, Naples and Fort Myers over 8 to 10 years (est. sellout $1.8B).
land_banking.note: Historical (2010): the only land-bank-style third-party capital found for GL. Business Observer's 2011 item links it to its own 'Land bankers on the prowl' story. No public evidence it is still active; most of those communities have since sold out.
